♯ FW !!! TIGER CANINES👀👀 ♯ Tigers possess 30 highly specialized teeth designed exclusively for a predatory lifestyle. Their upper jaw holds 16 teeth, while the lower jaw contains 14, only moving vertically without any side-to-side grinding. Dominating their mouth are the canine teeth, which grow between 2.5 and 4 inches (6.4 to 10 cm) long, making them the largest of any living cat species. These massive fangs are embedded with pressure-sensitive nerves that allow the tiger to feel exactly where to place a lethal bite to sever a victim's spinal cord or windpipe. A wide gap called a diastema separates these front weapons from the sharp, scissor-like carnassial teeth at the back, which shear meat into swallowable chunks without chewing. While born completely toothless, tigers quickly develop temporary milk teeth before their permanent adult set grows in to deliver an incredible bite force of up to 1,100 PSI ⌣  #tiger #canines #teeth #pantheriatigris #fyp

WHAT NEXT FOR GUATEMALA’S TIGERS? 🐯 Eight years. Seven survivors. One long-awaited rescue. Yesterday, ADI rescued seven tigers from the Rey Gitano Circus in Guatemala. After years of captivity and legal battles, they’re finally in our care. In 2018, ADI helped enforce Guatemala’s circus animal ban through an extraordinary 18-month mission, culminating in the airlift of 17 lions and tigers to the ADI Wildlife Sanctuary in South Africa. But one circus refused to let go. As the legal battle dragged on, animals tragically died or disappeared. Seven tigers survived, spending years confined to cages on circus trucks. Until yesterday. This “Homecoming” video captures the remarkable journey of those 17 rescued lions and tigers to sanctuary in South Africa. A glimpse of the future we’re fighting for once again. Space to roam. Room to heal. A life beyond the circus. For these seven survivors, a new chapter begins. Ahead lies veterinary care, recovery, rehabilitation, and the journey toward their forever home at the ADI Wildlife Sanctuary. The rescue is over. Their road to recovery starts with you.
